limitations: Synthetic touch *scrolling* could not be produced in this headless Chromium build (no GPU compositor): Input.dispatchTouchEvent delivers touch events to the page but produces no scroll, Input.synthesizeScrollGesture is inert, and wheel events over the plugin panel do not scroll it (all probed on this machine). Scrolling is therefore exercised through real scroll positions (scrollBy / scrollLeft), which is exactly what a settled swipe leaves behind: the CSS snap engine, the scroll→tab sync and the resting page are then the browser's own behaviour. Touch events themselves are dispatched for real and prove gesture delivery and the swipe-vs-tap guard.

The 390×844 / 844×390 viewports are emulated with an exact CSS viewport + touch points and a desktop UA (the plugin answers to viewport media queries only). The DSH shell keeps its desktop chrome, which is a host concern and out of the plugin scope.
